title: What are the three views of four joined cubes?
description: Four identical cubes are joined, three in a row on the floor and one on top of the left cube. The board looks from the front, from above and from the left side and draws each view, noticing which cubes are hidden. Keeko's doubt is that the top view has four squares.
teaching_notes: One idea: each view shows only the outline the eye meets from one direction, and a cube behind or below another is hidden. Watch for students who count every cube in every view.

source: Four identical cubes: three in a row on the floor, and one m
video_script.why: The child draws the views of joined cubes by asking which cubes the eye meets from each direction, because a cube hidden behind or below another shows no square of its own.
video_script.substitution: three cubes in a row on the floor and one on top of the left cube; front view an L of 4 squares; top view the top cube covers the cube under it, a row of 3 squares; side view from the left, the row hides behind the left cube, a column of 2 squares.
video_script.anchor: the four joined cubes with an eye at the front, above and at the left side
video_script.wrong_answer: there are four cubes, so the top view has four squares
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko counts all four cubes as four squares in the top view; the top cube sits right over the left cube and hides it, so the top view has only 3 squares, and the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The front view is an L of four squares. The top view is a row of three squares. The side view is a column of two squares

final_answer.value: Front: an L of 4 squares; top: a row of 3 squares; side: a column of 2 squares
final_answer.spoken: front, an L of four squares; top, a row of three squares; side, a column of two squares

hold_back: Front: an L of 4 squares; top: a row of 3 squares; side: a column of 2 squares
maths_rules: the front view is what the eye meets looking from the front, the top view from above, the side view from the left side
front view: 3 squares in a row with 1 square above the left one, an L of 4 squares
top view: the top cube covers the cube under it, so 3 squares in a row
side view from the left: the row hides behind the left cube, so a column of 2 squares
wrong idea: counting every cube in every view; hidden cubes show no square of their own
video_script.design: One idea: ask what the eye meets, and which cubes it cannot see. The four cubes sit on the stage and an eye moves to the front, above and the left side; hidden cubes dim while each view fills its own frame.
